deck.title: ECS, EKS & Fargate
deck.analogy: Containers are standardized steel shipping boxes for software, and an orchestrator (ECS/EKS) is the robotic harbor master directing the cranes.

subtopics.title: ECS vocabulary — learn these four words cold
The compute ladder (which service for which job)

cards.front: What is a container image in the context of ECS/EKS?

back.answer: Your app plus its entire environment (runtime, libraries, config, OS dependencies) packaged together so it runs identically anywhere.
back.explanation: This solves "it works on my machine".
back.mnemonic: A standardized steel shipping container for software.

cards.front: Where do containers sit on the compute spectrum versus Lambda and EC2?

back.answer: Middle ground: more control and longer-running than Lambda (no 15-minute limit), less babysitting than raw EC2.

cards.front: Why do you need a container orchestrator, and which two does AWS offer?

back.answer: To restart, spread, and wire up hundreds of containers: ECS (AWS's own, simple) and EKS (managed Kubernetes).
back.explanation: The orchestrator is the robotic harbor master.
back.mnemonic: Robotic harbor master directing the cranes.

cards.front: ECS: what is a Task Definition?

back.answer: A JSON blueprint: which image, CPU/RAM, ports, env vars, IAM roles.

cards.sourceHeading: ECS vocabulary — learn these four words cold

cards.front: ECS: what is a Task?

back.answer: One running copy of a task definition.
back.mnemonic: A dish cooked from the recipe.

cards.sourceHeading: ECS vocabulary — learn these four words cold

cards.front: ECS: what is a Service?

back.answer: Keeps N tasks running, replaces crashed ones, and wires them to an ALB.

cards.sourceHeading: ECS vocabulary — learn these four words cold

cards.front: ECS: what is a Cluster?

back.answer: A logical grouping of the infrastructure the tasks run on.

cards.sourceHeading: ECS vocabulary — learn these four words cold

cards.front: ECS/EKS EC2 launch type: what do you manage and what can you use?

back.answer: You manage the instances (types, patching, scaling); you can use Spot instances and attach GPUs.

cards.front: What is Fargate and what do you declare?

back.answer: Serverless containers: you declare CPU and memory per task; AWS provisions invisible compute.
back.explanation: "No server management" for containers means Fargate.

cards.front: Fargate trap: can Fargate run containerized ML inference that needs GPUs?

back.answer: No — Fargate does NOT support GPUs; use the EC2 launch type.
back.explanation: GPU needs always point to EC2 launch type.

cards.front: Is Fargate a third orchestrator alongside ECS and EKS?

back.answer: No — it's a compute layer that plugs into both ECS and EKS.
back.explanation: ECS/EKS decide what runs; Fargate is one option for where it runs.

cards.front: When should you choose EKS over ECS?

back.answer: Only when already using Kubernetes, or when portability/multi-cloud/avoiding vendor lock-in is required.
back.explanation: Otherwise default to ECS: simpler and AWS-native.

cards.front: ECS vs EKS: which is portable across clouds?

back.answer: EKS (Kubernetes runs anywhere); ECS is AWS-only.

cards.front: What is Amazon ECR?

back.answer: Elastic Container Registry: private, IAM-integrated storage for container images.
back.explanation: Like Docker Hub but private.

cards.front: Which ECR feature scans container images for CVEs?
ECS Task Execution Role: who uses it and for what?

back.answer: The ECS agent, for launching: pulling the image from ECR and writing logs to CloudWatch.
back.explanation: Wrong role shows as the task failing to start or being unable to pull the image.

cards.front: ECS Task Role: who uses it and for what?

back.answer: Your app code inside the container, for calls to S3, DynamoDB, SQS once running.
back.explanation: Wrong role shows as AccessDenied from the app.
back.mnemonic: Task Role = what the app does once it's up.

cards.front: What does ECS awsvpc network mode give each task?

back.answer: Its own ENI (private IP) and therefore its own security group; required on Fargate.

cards.front: What is ALB dynamic port mapping in ECS?

back.answer: On EC2 launch type, an ALB routes to multiple tasks of the same service on one instance, each on a random host port.
back.explanation: No manual port juggling.

cards.front: What metrics can ECS Service Auto Scaling use to scale task count?

back.answer: CPU, memory, or SQS queue depth.

cards.front: Run containers without managing any servers or clusters of instances. Which option?

back.explanation: "No server management" is the trigger.

choices.why: Serverless containers; no instances to manage.
Nodes are still yours to manage.

cards.front: A company runs Kubernetes on-premises and wants to migrate to AWS with minimal changes. Which service?

back.explanation: "Already Kubernetes" is an EKS signal.

cards.front: An ECS task fails to start with an error pulling the image from ECR. What is misconfigured?

back.explanation: Launch plumbing uses the execution role.

choices.why: Networking mode isn't the permission cause.
Needed by ECS agent to pull from ECR.

cards.front: An app inside an ECS container gets AccessDenied calling DynamoDB. What do you fix?

back.explanation: App-level permissions once running.

choices.why: Only for pulling images and logging.
Grants the app's own AWS API permissions.

cards.front: Containerized GPU-based ML inference, minimize management. Which launch option?

back.explanation: Fargate has no GPUs.

cards.front: Automatically scan container images for vulnerabilities. Which feature?

back.explanation: Built into the registry.

choices.why: Built-in CVE scanning in the registry.

cards.front: Assign a dedicated security group to each container/task. What do you use?

back.explanation: Per-task ENI means per-task SG.

choices.why: Each task gets its own ENI and SG.

cards.front: Avoid vendor lock-in; containers must be portable across clouds. Which service?

back.explanation: Kubernetes is the portability play.

cards.front: Cost-optimize fault-tolerant containerized batch jobs on Fargate. What option?

back.explanation: Interruptible workloads suit Spot.

cards.front: Scale container count based on messages waiting in a queue. What do you use?

back.answer: ECS Service Auto Scaling on SQS queue depth
back.explanation: Service Auto Scaling supports queue depth.

choices.text: ECS Service Auto Scaling on SQS queue depth
choices.why: Scales task count by queue backlog.
